title: DarkMe RAT Shifts to Phishing Distribution
headline: DarkMe RAT Shifts to Phishing Distribution
summary: DarkMe, a remote access trojan and info‑stealer linked to a threat group targeting traders and crypto users, now relies on simple phishing emails to deliver its first‑stage downloader. The approach replaces zero‑day exploits with social engineering, aiming to trick victims into running the malware on their machines.

title: Barracuda Launches AI‑Powered Data Security for Small Businesses
headline: Barracuda Launches AI‑Powered Data Security for Small Businesses
summary: Barracuda Networks unveiled Barracuda AI Data Security, an AI‑driven solution built on the BarracudaONE platform. It offers AI visibility, data protection, threat defense, and governance in a single package, enabling resource‑constrained organizations and MSPs to adopt AI responsibly while meeting compliance requirements.

title: Latvian Police Arrest Hacker Behind Electronics Repair Company Breach
headline: Latvian Police Arrest Hacker Behind Electronics Repair Company Breach
summary: Latvian police detained a 23‑year‑old suspect who allegedly hacked at least two electronics repair firms, stealing personal data and attempting to extort victims. The arrest follows investigations into unauthorized access and data theft. No public fix is required as the breach was contained by law enforcement.

title: UK Announces New Center to Counter State‑Sponsored Disinformation
headline: UK Announces New Center to Counter State‑Sponsored Disinformation
summary: The United Kingdom will establish a national center to detect, attribute, and disrupt hostile state disinformation. Prime Minister Andy Burnham unveiled the initiative at the UN General Assembly, aiming to strengthen defenses against state‑backed propaganda and protect public discourse.

title: Arista Patches Zero-Day Exploit in VeloCloud Orchestrator
headline: Arista Patches Zero-Day Exploit in VeloCloud Orchestrator
summary: Arista Networks released patches for a zero-day flaw actively exploited in VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) On‑Prem deployments. The vulnerability allows attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected systems. Users must apply the vendor’s update immediately to prevent exploitation.

title: cPanel Flaw Enables Root Code Execution and Server Takeover
headline: cPanel Flaw Enables Root Code Execution and Server Takeover
summary: A flaw in cPanel’s CalDAV and CardDAV services lets any hosting account run code as root, granting full server control. A separate issue in the WP Toolkit plugin allows account holders to modify other accounts’ databases. cPanel has issued fixed versions for both vulnerabilities.

title: XRanges Introduces AI Agent Scoring Tool
headline: XRanges Introduces AI Agent Scoring Tool
summary: XRanges is a new tool that lets security teams evaluate autonomous security agents by having them point at realistic targets and generate self‑written reports. Analysts then verify each claim, distinguishing real findings from false positives. The approach aims to improve confidence in AI‑driven bug‑finding systems.

title: Microsoft Disrupts AI‑Powered Phishing Platform EvilTokens
headline: Microsoft Disrupts AI‑Powered Phishing Platform EvilTokens
summary: Microsoft disrupted EvilTokens, an AI‑powered phishing platform that automates social engineering by generating targeted messages and selecting victims. The platform used machine learning to craft convincing emails and decide targets, enabling large‑scale phishing campaigns. Microsoft’s intervention halted the service, reducing the threat to potential victims.

title: Chrome 154 Patches 108 Vulnerabilities
headline: Chrome 154 Patches 108 Vulnerabilities
summary: Google Chrome version 154 addresses 108 critical memory safety and memory corruption flaws, including buffer overflows and use‑after‑free bugs. The update mitigates potential remote code execution risks. Users should install the patch immediately to protect against exploitation of these high‑severity vulnerabilities.

title: UAE, Saudi Arabia Absorb Half of Gulf Cyberattacks
headline: UAE, Saudi Arabia Absorb Half of Gulf Cyberattacks
summary: The United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia together absorbed half of all cyberattacks in the Gulf region during the first half of 2026, according to Dark Reading. This highlights a growing trend of complex attacks targeting the region’s critical infrastructure and businesses.

title: Honeywell: OT Security Teams Embrace AI, but Autonomy Still Rare
headline: Honeywell: OT Security Teams Embrace AI, but Autonomy Still Rare
summary: Honeywell reports that only 21% of industrial security leaders have a complete OT asset inventory, despite 88% claiming program maturity. The company notes that while AI is increasingly adopted in OT security, full operational autonomy remains rare, underscoring gaps in asset visibility and threat response.

title: Adobe Releases Patches for Nine Critical Flaws in Connect and AEM Forms
headline: Adobe Releases Patches for Nine Critical Flaws in Connect and AEM Forms
summary: Adobe has issued security updates for nine critical defects in its Connect and AEM Forms products that could allow attackers to execute arbitrary code and elevate privileges. The patches address the vulnerabilities and should be applied immediately to prevent potential exploitation.

title: Microsoft Windows 2026 Updates Disrupt Always On VPN on Windows 11
headline: Microsoft Windows 2026 Updates Disrupt Always On VPN on Windows 11
summary: Microsoft warned that the September 2026 security updates for Windows 11 may break Always On VPN connections on some systems. Users experiencing VPN failures should temporarily disable the updates or apply the vendor’s workaround until a fix is released.

title: Check Point Management Servers Hit by Critical RCE Vulnerabilities
headline: Check Point Management Servers Hit by Critical RCE Vulnerabilities
summary: Check Point released emergency fixes for a critical Check Point Management Server vulnerability (CVE-2026-93616) exploited since July 23, 2026, and a pre-authentication RCE in Check Point (Quantum) Security Gateway (CVE-2026-85102) probed shortly after patch release. Patches were issued on September 9, 2026.

title: OpenAI Launches GPT-6 Sol and Luna Models with Lower API Prices
headline: OpenAI Launches GPT-6 Sol and Luna Models with Lower API Prices
summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, available in ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the desktop app for various user tiers. The models are accessible via the API as gpt-6-sol and gpt-6-luna, with a phased rollout to maintain stability.

title: F5 BIG‑IP APM Unauthenticated RCE Exploited on OAuth Servers
headline: F5 BIG‑IP APM Unauthenticated RCE Exploited on OAuth Servers
summary: F5 BIG‑IP Access Policy Manager (APM) systems that act as OAuth authorization servers are vulnerable to an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw (CVE‑2026‑94127). Attackers can run arbitrary code without logging in, potentially issuing malicious tokens. F5 released an engineering hotfix on September 22. Apply the patch immediately to prevent exploitation.

title: Chinese Threat Actor Exploits Chrome‑Windows Zero‑Day Chain to Deploy CLEANGULP Malware
headline: Chinese Threat Actor Exploits Chrome‑Windows Zero‑Day Chain to Deploy CLEANGULP Malware
summary: Chinese threat actor UTA0565 exploited a chain of zero‑day vulnerabilities in Google Chrome and Windows (CVE‑2026‑85046, CVE‑2026‑87491, CVE‑2026‑85880) via fake websites to deploy CLEANGULP malware. The attacks were detected on September 3 and 4, 2026. The chain allows remote code execution on victim machines, enabling malware installation.

title: Ryuk Ransomware Operator Sentenced to 24 Months
headline: Ryuk Ransomware Operator Sentenced to 24 Months
summary: An Armenian man was sentenced to 24 months in prison and 3 years of supervised release for hacking U.S. companies and encrypting their systems in Ryuk ransomware attacks.

title: Critical F5 BIG‑IP Vulnerability Enables Remote Code Execution
headline: Critical F5 BIG‑IP Vulnerability Enables Remote Code Execution
summary: Unauthenticated attackers can send crafted traffic to F5 BIG‑IP devices, triggering remote code execution. The flaw allows full system compromise without authentication. No CVE ID is disclosed. Immediate patching is required to prevent exploitation.

title: F5 Releases Patches for BIG‑IP APM Zero‑Day Exploited in RCE Attacks
headline: F5 Releases Patches for BIG‑IP APM Zero‑Day Exploited in RCE Attacks
summary: F5 issued security updates for a critical BIG‑IP APM zero‑day vulnerability being used in remote code execution attacks. The flaw permits attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected devices. Applying the latest patches mitigates the risk.

title: ShinyHunters Accuses FBI of Hack, Threatens Leak of Stolen Data
headline: ShinyHunters Accuses FBI of Hack, Threatens Leak of Stolen Data
summary: The cybercrime group ShinyHunters claims the FBI hacked them and demands a retraction of a threat report. They threaten to leak stolen information if the report is not retracted. The incident highlights potential data exposure from law enforcement investigations.

title: Next.js ImageResponse Vulnerability Enables Server Code Execution via SVG
headline: Next.js ImageResponse Vulnerability Enables Server Code Execution via SVG
summary: A critical flaw in Next.js’s ImageResponse feature allows attackers to execute server-side code by supplying crafted SVG input. The vulnerability occurs when untrusted data, such as request URL text, is rendered into images. Vercel patched the issue on September 22 in the latest Next.js release.

title: Prismor: Open-Source Runtime Control Plane for AI Agents
headline: Prismor: Open-Source Runtime Control Plane for AI Agents
summary: Prismor is a free, open‑source security layer that sits between AI coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor and the actions they execute. It evaluates each tool call against a policy, returning allow, warn, or block. The layer protects against malicious or unintended shell commands, file access, and credential exposure.

title: ShinyHunters Claims FBI Breach, Stole Data on Agents and Job Applicants
headline: ShinyHunters Claims FBI Breach, Stole Data on Agents and Job Applicants
summary: ShinyHunters, a cyber‑extortion group, claims it breached the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation and stole data on current and former FBI employees and job applicants. The group asserts it holds sensitive information on nearly all FBI agents and applicants. The breach exposes personnel data and could compromise national security.

title: Savi’s Scamwise Service Scans Messages, URLs, and Phone Numbers for Fraud
headline: Savi’s Scamwise Service Scans Messages, URLs, and Phone Numbers for Fraud
summary: Savi’s free Scamwise tool scans suspicious emails, websites, phone numbers, images, and real‑world scenarios for fraud indicators. It runs in any web browser on desktop, mobile, or tablet without an account and is also part of the Savi iOS and Android app, currently available only in the United States.

title: Nearly Two-Thirds of Tested Websites Fail Bot Tests
headline: Nearly Two-Thirds of Tested Websites Fail Bot Tests
summary: DataDome’s 2026 State of Bot & Agent Security Report shows that almost 66% of 75,000 customer sites failed every bot test. Bot traffic rose 124% from July 2025 to June 2026, while human traffic grew only 13.2%. AI agent and LLM crawler traffic increased 82.3%, nine times faster than human traffic.

title: CVE-2026-87121 Out-of-Bounds Write in lwIP MQTT Client Enables Full Code Execution
headline: CVE-2026-87121 Out-of-Bounds Write in lwIP MQTT Client Enables Full Code Execution
summary: The CVE-2026-87121 vulnerability in the lwIP TCP/IP Stack MQTT Client Application (versions >=2.0.1) allows an attacker to perform an out-of-bounds write, potentially leading to full code execution on affected devices. The flaw impacts critical infrastructure sectors worldwide. Mitigation requires updating to a patched lwIP version.

title: Attackers Impersonate AI Brands to Distribute Malware
headline: Attackers Impersonate AI Brands to Distribute Malware
summary: Attackers are exploiting the popularity of AI tools by impersonating well‑known AI brands to distribute malware. Sophos MDR casework shows repeated use of malvertising and infostealer tactics. The campaign targets users seeking AI solutions, delivering malicious payloads that steal credentials and other sensitive data.

title: DecryptAds Reveals Who Is Tracking Users Across Web and Mobile
headline: DecryptAds Reveals Who Is Tracking Users Across Web and Mobile
summary: DecryptAds is a free, open‑source service that scrapes ad‑tech data to reveal the entities tracking users across websites and mobile apps. By correlating publicly available information, it allows individuals to quickly identify advertisers, data brokers, and other trackers, simplifying privacy investigations and enhancing transparency.

title: Microsoft Releases Patch for 398 Windows Vulnerabilities, One Actively Exploited
headline: Microsoft Releases Patch for 398 Windows Vulnerabilities, One Actively Exploited
summary: Microsoft issued updates fixing 398 security flaws in Windows and related software, including a vulnerability already under active exploitation. The patch addresses multiple weaknesses, some previously disclosed, and mitigates potential attack vectors across the operating system and supported applications.

title: Adobe August 2026 Patch Rollout Covers 51 CVEs Across Multiple Products
headline: Adobe August 2026 Patch Rollout Covers 51 CVEs Across Multiple Products
summary: Adobe released five bulletins in August 2026, addressing 51 unique CVEs in ColdFusion, Commerce, Lightroom Classic, Content Credentials SDK, and Campaign Classic. The updates patch critical security flaws across these products, reducing exposure to known exploits and strengthening overall platform security.

title: Rabbit Releases Cloud‑Based OS3 That Controls User Laptops
headline: Rabbit Releases Cloud‑Based OS3 That Controls User Laptops
summary: Rabbit released OS3, an agentic operating system that runs in the cloud and controls a user’s laptop via a local agent installed with one command. Users issue goals in chat; OS3 selects the device and automates desktop software, file access, web browsing, or code execution. One account can connect up to five devices.

title: NetBSD 10.2 Patch Fixes Remote Kernel Crash in ipfilter
headline: NetBSD 10.2 Patch Fixes Remote Kernel Crash in ipfilter
summary: A NetBSD 10.2 system exposed a remotely triggerable null pointer dereference in the ipfilter kernel module, allowing an external attacker to cause a kernel crash. The NetBSD Project released a patch on September 15, fixing the flaw and preventing potential denial‑of‑service attacks.

title: ShinyHunters Claims FBI Breach via PeopleSoft Zero-Day
headline: ShinyHunters Claims FBI Breach via PeopleSoft Zero-Day
summary: ShinyHunters alleges it exploited a zero‑day flaw in PeopleSoft to breach FBI systems, reportedly exfiltrating 3 TB of employee and applicant data. The group claims the attack enabled unauthorized access to sensitive records, but no official confirmation or remediation details have been released.

title: Cyera Secures $400 Million Series G Funding
headline: Cyera Secures $400 Million Series G Funding
summary: Cyera, a data security firm, closed a $400 million Series G round led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives, valuing the company at over $12 billion. The investment expands Cyera’s capital base to support growth and product development, with no immediate operational impact reported.

title: Siemens SIMOVE Fleetmanager and SIPLANT Path Traversal Vulnerability (CVE-2026-67367)
headline: Siemens SIMOVE Fleetmanager and SIPLANT Path Traversal Vulnerability (CVE-2026-67367)
summary: Siemens SIMOVE Fleetmanager and SIPLANT versions V3.1 to V4.0 and V1.7 to V3.1 contain a relative path traversal flaw (CVE-2026-67367) that could allow attackers to read files outside intended directories. Siemens released patches; users should update to the latest versions immediately.

title: Siemens Siveillance Control Unrestricted File Upload Vulnerability
headline: Siemens Siveillance Control Unrestricted File Upload Vulnerability
summary: A vulnerability in the Open Interface Services web module of Siemens Siveillance Control and Pro allows attackers to upload arbitrary files, potentially leading to root-level access on the OIS server. Siemens has released patches and recommends updating to the latest versions to mitigate the risk.

title: Sweden Fines Miljödata $183K for 2.2M Citizen Data Breach
headline: Sweden Fines Miljödata $183K for 2.2M Citizen Data Breach
summary: Sweden’s privacy watchdog IMY fined software vendor Miljödata $183,000 under GDPR Article 32 after an extortion breach exposed 2.2 million citizen records. The fine reflects the vendor’s failure to protect personal data and comply with GDPR security requirements.

title: Chinese Hackers Use WordPress and Zyxel Flaws to Steal Government Records
headline: Chinese Hackers Use WordPress and Zyxel Flaws to Steal Government Records
summary: Chinese threat actors breached 49 organizations in 29 countries by chaining WordPress and Zyxel vulnerabilities. They stole over 18,500 sensitive government records, demonstrating a coordinated state-sponsored attack that leveraged multiple software weaknesses.

title: Chinese Hackers Exploit ZyXEL and WordPress Vulnerabilities to Steal Government Data
headline: Chinese Hackers Exploit ZyXEL and WordPress Vulnerabilities to Steal Government Data
summary: A Chinese-speaking threat actor has leveraged security flaws in ZyXEL GS1900 Smart Managed Switches and WordPress to exfiltrate sensitive data from 996 devices and over 18,500 backend database records. The attack targeted government networks, compromising confidential information.

title: VeloCloud Orchestrator CVE-2026-93952 Exploited in Certificate-Based Setups
headline: VeloCloud Orchestrator CVE-2026-93952 Exploited in Certificate-Based Setups
summary: Arista reports attackers exploiting CVE-2026-93952 in on‑premises VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO). The flaw allows remote attackers without login to gain privileged internal functions on the VCO host, affecting setups that authenticate Edge devices with certificates. No fix or mitigation is provided in the report.

title: Siemens SIPLUS and SIMATIC Products Vulnerable to Copy Fail (CVE-2026-31431)
headline: Siemens SIPLUS and SIMATIC Products Vulnerable to Copy Fail (CVE-2026-31431)
summary: Siemens SIPLUS and SIMATIC products are affected by the Copy Fail vulnerability (CVE-2026-31431). Affected versions include SIMATIC AX Runtime Core Linux Common Debian, ARM64, Platform Container, VMWare Development, and certain HMI MTP1000 models. Siemens has released updated firmware and recommends applying the latest patches or implementing countermeasures where fixes are pending.

title: Siemens Desigo CC Client Code Execution Vulnerability (CVE-2026-34223)
headline: Siemens Desigo CC Client Code Execution Vulnerability (CVE-2026-34223)
summary: A Client Code Execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-34223) in Siemens Desigo CC allows attackers to run arbitrary code on client devices via specially crafted graphics documents containing embedded scripts. Successful exploitation can compromise the client OS and enable lateral movement. Affected versions V6 and V7 have patches available; users should update immediately.

title: Rogue MFA Providers Can Steal Passwords During Logins
headline: Rogue MFA Providers Can Steal Passwords During Logins
summary: Researchers showed how attackers with privileged access can register a fake external MFA provider that intercepts users’ passwords during legitimate login attempts. The technique exploits MFA registration flows, allowing credential theft without detection. Mitigation requires verifying MFA provider authenticity and restricting privileged account permissions.

title: Sweden Fines Miljödata $183,000 Over Breach Affecting 2.2 Million
headline: Sweden Fines Miljödata $183,000 Over Breach Affecting 2.2 Million
summary: Sweden’s data privacy regulator IMY fined IT systems provider Miljödata SEK 1.8 million ($183,000) for inadequate security that caused a breach in August 2025 affecting 2.2 million individuals. The incident exposed personal data, prompting regulatory action and highlighting the need for stronger safeguards and compliance.

title: Chinese Users Mask Identities to Access US AI Models via Relay Servers
headline: Chinese Users Mask Identities to Access US AI Models via Relay Servers
summary: Over 80,000 relay servers are enabling Chinese users to conceal their identities while accessing advanced large language models in the United States, likely for model cloning purposes. The widespread use of these relays highlights a growing trend of cross‑border AI model exploitation and raises concerns about intellectual property protection.

title: Microsoft Seizes 50 Sites to Shut Down EvilTokens Phishing‑as‑a‑Service
headline: Microsoft Seizes 50 Sites to Shut Down EvilTokens Phishing‑as‑a‑Service
summary: Microsoft disrupted the EvilTokens phishing‑as‑a‑service platform by seizing 50 websites and disabling more than 150 domains. The service targeted Microsoft 365 accounts, enabling attackers to harvest credentials. The shutdown stops the distribution of phishing kits and reduces the risk of credential theft for Microsoft users.

title: Critical Bifrost AI Gateway Flaw Lets Attackers Run Commands Without Credentials
headline: Critical Bifrost AI Gateway Flaw Lets Attackers Run Commands Without Credentials
summary: A critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-90898) in Bifrost, an open‑source AI gateway, allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands via a single HTTP request. The flaw affects all Bifrost HTTP transport versions before 2.1.0 when management authentication is disabled. Immediate patching is required.

title: Researcher Drops BigDiskBuster Zero‑Day PoC That Blocks Microsoft Defender Updates
headline: Researcher Drops BigDiskBuster Zero‑Day PoC That Blocks Microsoft Defender Updates
summary: A zero‑day proof‑of‑concept tool named BigDiskBuster fills disk space to halt Microsoft Defender from installing platform and signature updates. Published on GitHub, it has no patch, CVE, or Microsoft advisory. The tool exploits a resource exhaustion flaw, preventing update processes and potentially leaving systems vulnerable.

title: lwIP (Lightweight IP) Double Free Vulnerability CVE-2026-91018
headline: lwIP (Lightweight IP) Double Free Vulnerability CVE-2026-91018
summary: The lwIP (Lightweight IP) library versions API >=2.0.1 contain a double free flaw (CVE-2026-91018) that can cause a system crash, denial of service, memory corruption, or remote code execution. Affected systems include critical infrastructure sectors worldwide. Mitigation requires updating to the latest patched release.

title: Siemens WTV676 and WTV776 Denial of Service Vulnerability CVE-2026-89207
headline: Siemens WTV676 and WTV776 Denial of Service Vulnerability CVE-2026-89207
summary: Siemens WTV676 and WTV776 devices have a denial of service flaw (CVE-2026-89207) where improper input validation can force the devices into protection mode, disabling remote web access. Siemens recommends updating to the latest firmware versions to remediate the issue.

title: Canadian Regulator Investigates IDScan Over Data Privacy Allegations
headline: Canadian Regulator Investigates IDScan Over Data Privacy Allegations
summary: The Canadian privacy regulator has opened a probe into IDScan, alleging violations of federal private‑sector privacy law. The investigation will examine IDScan’s security practices and whether victim notifications met legal requirements. No specific breach has been reported, but the probe could lead to enforcement action.

title: Malicious npm Package 'tw-pkgprobe-7731' Steals Credentials
headline: Malicious npm Package 'tw-pkgprobe-7731' Steals Credentials
summary: Researchers uncovered a malicious npm package named tw‑pkgprobe‑7731 that masquerades as a Twilio bug‑bounty tool. The package, uploaded in mid‑August 2026, stealthily harvests credentials from developers’ environments. The threat remains active on the npm registry, and users should delete the package and audit dependencies.

title: Wazuh Reduces Shadow IT Visibility Gaps
headline: Wazuh Reduces Shadow IT Visibility Gaps
summary: Wazuh offers endpoint inventory, agentless monitoring, and centralized analysis to help security teams detect unmanaged endpoints, unauthorized software, and other assets outside existing monitoring, reducing shadow IT visibility gaps.

title: Microsoft Takedown of EvilTokens Phishing Service
headline: Microsoft Takedown of EvilTokens Phishing Service
summary: Microsoft dismantled the EvilTokens device-code phishing service, which used AI throughout its attack chain, after a U.S. court order. The takedown involved Health-ISAC, Cloudflare, Coinbase, OpenAI, Railway, SpyCloud, and The Shadowserver, stopping 12,000 compromised inboxes.

title: Check Point Issues Emergency Hotfix for Critical Management Server Zero‑Day
headline: Check Point Issues Emergency Hotfix for Critical Management Server Zero‑Day
summary: Check Point released emergency hotfixes for a critical Security Management Server vulnerability that could allow attackers to run arbitrary scripts. The flaw enables remote code execution on affected servers, potentially compromising network management and control. Patching is mandatory to prevent exploitation.

title: OpenPLC Runtime v3 Vulnerability Allows Session Hijacking and Control of PLCs
headline: OpenPLC Runtime v3 Vulnerability Allows Session Hijacking and Control of PLCs
summary: A critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-88020) in OpenPLC Runtime v3 lets attackers hijack session cookies and issue state‑changing requests, enabling full control over programmable logic controllers and the physical processes they manage. Affected versions include OpenPLC 3. Users should apply vendor patches immediately.

title: CISA Adds Four Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
headline: CISA Adds Four Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
summary: CISA has added four new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, citing active exploitation. The catalog lists CVE-2026-85102, CVE-2026-93616, CVE-2026-93952, and CVE-2026-94127, covering certificate validation, path traversal, input validation, and a heap‑based buffer overflow in Check Point, Arista, and F5 products.

title: Industrial Organizations Rank Cybersecurity Risk as Top Growth Obstacle
headline: Industrial Organizations Rank Cybersecurity Risk as Top Growth Obstacle
summary: A recent study shows that over one third of industrial organizations view cybersecurity risk as a primary barrier to growth, prompting increased investment in security as connected operations, AI adoption, and IT/OT convergence expand operational risk.

title: Scammers Use Real Google Sign‑In Screens to Sell Fake AI Subscriptions
headline: Scammers Use Real Google Sign‑In Screens to Sell Fake AI Subscriptions
summary: Scammers employ a $249 toolkit to create over 100 fake AI subscription sites that mimic legitimate Google sign‑in screens, convincing users to pay up to $2,000 annually for unverified services. Malwarebytes linked all sites to the same developer and toolkit, exposing a widespread phishing operation.

title: Japan Dismantles First North Korean Laptop Farm as Allies Reveal Wider Scheme
headline: Japan Dismantles First North Korean Laptop Farm as Allies Reveal Wider Scheme
summary: Japan dismantled a North Korean laptop farm, part of the WaterPlum campaign. A joint US, Japan, Germany, and Australia report details the broader scheme, indicating coordinated state-sponsored espionage targeting global infrastructure.

title: Microsoft Disrupts EvilTokens PhaaS After 12,000 Accounts Breached
headline: Microsoft Disrupts EvilTokens PhaaS After 12,000 Accounts Breached
summary: Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit and international partners disrupted the EvilTokens PhaaS platform after it hijacked over 12,000 enterprise cloud accounts, exposing sensitive data and compromising access to corporate resources. The takedown stops further credential theft and limits ongoing exploitation of the compromised accounts.

title: ShinyHunters Claims FBI Hack via Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Day
headline: ShinyHunters Claims FBI Hack via Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Day
summary: ShinyHunters claims to have breached FBI systems via a new Oracle PeopleSoft zero‑day vulnerability, accessing internal services and exfiltrating sensitive employee and job applicant data. The gang alleges the exploit bypassed security controls, enabling data theft before detection. No CVE ID is disclosed.

title: Check Point Warns of Management Server Zero-Day Exploited in Targeted Attacks
headline: Check Point Warns of Management Server Zero-Day Exploited in Targeted Attacks
summary: Check Point disclosed that attackers exploited CVE-2026-93616, a zero‑day flaw in its Security Management Server, on July 23. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated script execution via the server’s web service. A patch was released on September 22 to protect firewall policy management.

title: New ClosedQuorum Windows Malware Uses AI for Attack Decisions
headline: New ClosedQuorum Windows Malware Uses AI for Attack Decisions
summary: ClosedQuorum is a Windows malware that leverages Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, and Mistral AI models to autonomously decide post‑compromise actions. The tool enhances decision‑making during attacks, potentially increasing effectiveness and stealth.

title: WordPress Releases Patch for Critical Code Execution Flaw
headline: WordPress Releases Patch for Critical Code Execution Flaw
summary: WordPress fixed a critical core flaw that allows unauthenticated attackers to load external PHP files and, on some servers, execute arbitrary code. The patch was released on September 22 in WordPress 7.1.2 and applies to all supported branches back to 4.7. Site owners are urged to update immediately.

title: BigCommerce Customer Data Stolen via Compromised Ribon App Key
headline: BigCommerce Customer Data Stolen via Compromised Ribon App Key
summary: Attackers exploited a compromised application key in Ribon, a third‑party BigCommerce app, to access and exfiltrate customer data. The breach highlights the risk of third‑party integrations and the need for strict key management and monitoring.

title: Shai-Hulud Attack Compromises CrowdSec GitHub Repositories
headline: Shai-Hulud Attack Compromises CrowdSec GitHub Repositories
summary: Threat actors used a stolen OAuth token from a former employee’s machine to access 170 private CrowdSec GitHub repositories. The token was obtained via the TanStack npm supply chain attack. The breach exposed internal code and potentially sensitive data, requiring immediate token revocation and repository audit.

title: AI Safety Debate Intensifies Amid Rising Misalignment Incidents
headline: AI Safety Debate Intensifies Amid Rising Misalignment Incidents
summary: Increasing reports of AI misalignment incidents are prompting large AI labs, businesses, and governments to seek stronger control mechanisms. The debate focuses on developing safeguards to prevent unintended AI behavior and ensuring secure deployment of advanced models.

title: VeloCloud Orchestrator CVE-2026-93952 Exploited for Remote Code Execution
headline: VeloCloud Orchestrator CVE-2026-93952 Exploited for Remote Code Execution
summary: A CVSS 10.0 flaw (CVE-2026-93952) in VeloCloud Orchestrator is actively exploited, allowing attackers to execute pre‑auth remote code across enterprise SD‑WANs. The vulnerability enables full system compromise without authentication. Immediate patching is required to mitigate the high‑risk threat.

title: Siemens Industrial Edge Management Authentication Bypass Vulnerability (CVE-2026-18963)
headline: Siemens Industrial Edge Management Authentication Bypass Vulnerability (CVE-2026-18963)
summary: Siemens Industrial Edge Management has an authentication bypass flaw allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to reset credentials and take over accounts without email verification. Affected versions include all Cloud, Pro V1 ≥1.14.9, Pro V2 ≥2.2.0, and Virtual ≥2.6.0. Siemens released patches; users must update immediately.

title: Microsoft SharePoint CVE-2026-65660 Enables In-Memory Pre-Auth Remote Code Execution
headline: Microsoft SharePoint CVE-2026-65660 Enables In-Memory Pre-Auth Remote Code Execution
summary: Microsoft SharePoint flaw CVE-2026-65660 misclassified as spoofing allows both authenticated and pre-authenticated attackers to execute remote code in memory. The vulnerability can be exploited without user interaction, enabling attackers to run arbitrary code on affected SharePoint servers. Microsoft has issued a patch to remediate the issue.

title: UK Arrests Two Over EvilTokens AI-Chatbot Used to Compromise Accounts
headline: UK Arrests Two Over EvilTokens AI-Chatbot Used to Compromise Accounts
summary: Two individuals were arrested in the UK after the takedown of the EvilTokens AI-chatbot, which charged a $1,500 initiation fee and $500 monthly subscription. The bot supplied cybercriminals with AI tools to compromise accounts, analyze breached inboxes, and identify monetization methods. The operation targeted fraud and account takeover activities.

title: EvilTokens PhaaS Disrupted After Compromising 12,000 Microsoft Accounts
headline: EvilTokens PhaaS Disrupted After Compromising 12,000 Microsoft Accounts
summary: Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit disrupted the EvilTokens PhaaS platform after it compromised over 12,000 Microsoft accounts across more than 10,000 organizations. The operation halted the platform’s infrastructure, preventing further token theft and device code phishing attacks.

title: Microsoft Disrupts EvilTokens Infrastructure to Stop Device Code Phishing
headline: Microsoft Disrupts EvilTokens Infrastructure to Stop Device Code Phishing
summary: Microsoft Digital Crimes Unit dismantled EvilTokens’ infrastructure, a leading PhaaS platform used for device code phishing. The disruption stopped automated AI‑assisted lures and token theft operations, protecting users from credential compromise.

title: New HTTP Query Method Allows GET Requests with Body
headline: New HTTP Query Method Allows GET Requests with Body
summary: A new HTTP Query method has been introduced to permit GET requests to include a body, addressing the limitation that GET requests traditionally lack bodies. The method aims to expand functionality while maintaining standard HTTP semantics. No security impact or vulnerability is reported.

title: Cloudflare Adds Vary Header Support to Cache Rules
headline: Cloudflare Adds Vary Header Support to Cache Rules
summary: Cloudflare now supports the Vary header in Cache Rules across all plans, allowing normalization of negotiation headers, passing exact values to the origin, or bypassing cache when variations are unpredictable. This feature improves cache accuracy for dynamic content.

title: Cisco Talos Releases CAIRN to Detect AI‑Driven Malware
headline: Cisco Talos Releases CAIRN to Detect AI‑Driven Malware
summary: Talos unveiled CAIRN, an open‑source framework that classifies and analyzes AI‑based malware using only file metadata. By linking binaries through attributes like submitter, import hash, domain, or AI provider, CAIRN helps security teams identify and track evolving threats without executing code.

title: Elsevier Domains Hijacked, Redirected to LAPSUS$ Page
headline: Elsevier Domains Hijacked, Redirected to LAPSUS$ Page
summary: Elsevier’s three Dutch academic publishing domains were hijacked, redirecting visitors to a LAPSUS$ “Chapter II” page that taunted the FBI and warned of a future victim. The redirect lasted at least 78 minutes, from 7:49 pm CT to before 10:09 pm CT on September 21, 2026. Elsevier has not yet explained how the hijack occurred.

title: Nightmare Eclipse Leaks New Microsoft Defender Exploit, Reveals Identity
headline: Nightmare Eclipse Leaks New Microsoft Defender Exploit, Reveals Identity
summary: Nightmare Eclipse, a former Microsoft Germany employee, disclosed a new exploit targeting Microsoft Defender and revealed his identity. The leak exposes a vulnerability that could allow attackers to bypass Defender protections, but no details on the specific flaw or mitigation are provided in the initial report.

title: Windows Defender Zero‑Day Exploit Blocks Antivirus Updates
headline: Windows Defender Zero‑Day Exploit Blocks Antivirus Updates
summary: Security researcher Abdelhamid Naceri disclosed BigDiskBuster, an unprivileged Windows Defender zero‑day that permanently blocks antivirus updates. The exploit prevents the Defender service from downloading or installing new signatures, leaving systems vulnerable to emerging threats. No patch is available yet; users should disable Defender or use alternative protection until a fix is released.

title: AI Agents Challenge Traditional Lateral Movement Controls
headline: AI Agents Challenge Traditional Lateral Movement Controls
summary: Security teams are rethinking access controls as AI agents autonomously discover new lateral movement paths. Unlike deterministic applications, AI agents relentlessly pursue tasks, potentially exploiting any available privilege. The trend highlights the need for dynamic monitoring and adaptive defenses to detect and block AI‑driven lateral movement before it compromises critical assets.

title: AI Advantage Skewed Toward Attackers, Warns UK NCSC CTO
headline: AI Advantage Skewed Toward Attackers, Warns UK NCSC CTO
summary: The NCSC CTO Dave Chismon warned that AI’s rapid advancement will favor attackers over defenders, as automated attacks outpace defensive tools. He highlighted the growing imbalance in AI capabilities, suggesting that cyberattacks will increase as defenses struggle to keep pace. No immediate fix is offered.

title: Cloudflare Launches Worker Previews for Isolated Branch Testing
headline: Cloudflare Launches Worker Previews for Isolated Branch Testing
summary: Worker Previews, a new Cloudflare feature, creates isolated preview environments for each branch of a worker. Each preview gets its own URL, configuration, state, and observability, allowing developers and agents to test changes in parallel without impacting production. This improves deployment safety and debugging.

title: D-Link Issues Critical Zero‑Day Alert for DIR‑822A Routers
headline: D-Link Issues Critical Zero‑Day Alert for DIR‑822A Routers
summary: D‑Link has warned that its legacy DIR‑822A dual‑band Wi‑Fi routers contain a maximum‑severity vulnerability identified as CVE‑2026‑86296. Public proof‑of‑concept exploit code is available, but no patch has been released. Users should immediately disconnect affected devices or apply a firmware update when one becomes available.

title: Only 13% of OT Network Segments Are Fully Isolated, Study Finds
headline: Only 13% of OT Network Segments Are Fully Isolated, Study Finds
summary: A new Forescout study reveals that just 13% of operational technology (OT) and medical device network segments are fully isolated from other enterprise assets. The research highlights widespread shared segments, increasing risk of lateral movement and potential compromise across critical infrastructure environments.

title: SharePoint Server Authenticated RCE via CVE-2026-65660
headline: SharePoint Server Authenticated RCE via CVE-2026-65660
summary: Microsoft’s SharePoint Server 2016, 2019, and Subscription Edition are vulnerable to authenticated remote code execution through CVE-2026-65660, originally classified as a spoofing flaw. The flaw allows attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server. Patches are available; administrators should apply them immediately.

title: Zyxel GS1900 Switches Compromised via CVE-2026-7273
headline: Zyxel GS1900 Switches Compromised via CVE-2026-7273
summary: A threat actor exploited CVE-2026-7273 in unpatched ZyXEL GS1900 Smart Managed Switches, compromising 996 devices in 48 countries. The vulnerability enabled data exfiltration from the switches. Operators should update firmware to the latest version and monitor network traffic for suspicious activity.

title: AI Bots Increasing POST Requests on E-commerce and Travel Sites
headline: AI Bots Increasing POST Requests on E-commerce and Travel Sites
summary: Akamai observed that AI crawlers, including ChatGPT, are moving beyond passive browsing to high‑frequency POST requests, with 44.8% targeting e‑commerce and 30% targeting travel sites. These POST actions can trigger actions such as logins or cart additions, potentially enabling malicious exploitation if sites lack proper input validation.

title: WordPress Fixes Remote Code Execution Vulnerability in Theme Installation
headline: WordPress Fixes Remote Code Execution Vulnerability in Theme Installation
summary: WordPress released a patch for a flaw that allowed attackers to automatically install and preview themes, leading to remote code execution. The vulnerability enabled malicious code to run on affected sites during theme handling, compromising site integrity. The update mitigates the issue by tightening theme installation controls.

title: Malicious npm Package 'indexed-btree' Hides Loader in Runtime Code
headline: Malicious npm Package 'indexed-btree' Hides Loader in Runtime Code
summary: A malicious npm package named "indexed-btree" was found hiding its loader within application code instead of using lifecycle scripts, a tactic shift in response to security controls. The package mimics the legitimate "sorted-btree" utility, potentially enabling stealthy code execution in Node.js projects.

title: Deepfake Social Engineering Increases, 41% of CISOs Reported Incidents
headline: Deepfake Social Engineering Increases, 41% of CISOs Reported Incidents
summary: A Gartner survey shows 41% of CISOs experienced deepfake social engineering during employee audio calls and 36% during video calls in the past year. The study highlights rising deepfake threats, with 79% reporting phishing or business email compromise and 58% vishing or smishing incidents, underscoring the need for robust verification protocols.

title: IP Theft Tactics Shift Toward CEO‑Like Impersonation
headline: IP Theft Tactics Shift Toward CEO‑Like Impersonation
summary: CSC’s State of Online IP Risk 2026 report identifies impersonation, phishing, and domain‑name abuse as top IP infringement methods. The study surveyed 300 IP law executives, noting that online marketplaces, paid search, and branded content are primary targets, and highlights operational challenges in managing these evolving threats.

title: Chinese Hackers Exploit ZyXEL Switch Vulnerability to Exfiltrate Data
headline: Chinese Hackers Exploit ZyXEL Switch Vulnerability to Exfiltrate Data
summary: Chinese threat actors exploited a vulnerability in ZyXEL network switches, exfiltrating sensitive data from nearly 1,000 devices. The flaw allowed remote code execution, enabling attackers to read configuration files and network traffic. No patch details provided; administrators should update firmware and monitor logs.

title: DORA Year Two Challenges SOC Visibility for Financial Institutions
headline: DORA Year Two Challenges SOC Visibility for Financial Institutions
summary: In its second year, the Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) forces EU financial entities to demonstrate real‑time SOC visibility into cyber incidents. Firms must document escalation workflows, assess third‑party risk, and prove that security operations can detect and respond to threats under the new regulatory framework.

title: Linux Kernel KVM ARM64 Flaw Exposes Host Memory to Guests
headline: Linux Kernel KVM ARM64 Flaw Exposes Host Memory to Guests
summary: A flaw in Linux kernel KVM virtualization for ARM64 processors, CVE-2026-89775, allows a guest VM to read and write host kernel memory on systems with nested virtualization. The vulnerability can be leveraged to escape the guest and execute code on the host, posing a severe security risk.

title: Malicious NPM Package 'indexed-btree' Disguises Malware Trigger
headline: Malicious NPM Package 'indexed-btree' Disguises Malware Trigger
summary: The npm package indexed-btree, posing as the legitimate sorted-btree, contains a hidden malware trigger in its prototype method. The malicious code can be downloaded millions of times, potentially compromising any project that installs the package and enabling attackers to execute arbitrary code.

title: Microsoft Defender Zero-Day Blocks Antivirus Updates
headline: Microsoft Defender Zero-Day Blocks Antivirus Updates
summary: A new zero-day exploit in Microsoft Defender, discovered by researcher Abdelhamid Naceri, prevents Windows Defender from downloading or installing updates. The flaw stops the antivirus from receiving critical patches, leaving systems vulnerable to known threats. No official CVE ID is disclosed. Users should disable automatic updates and apply manual patches as soon as available.

title: CISA Urges Patch of Zyxel Switch Flaw Used for Data Theft
headline: CISA Urges Patch of Zyxel Switch Flaw Used for Data Theft
summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency has issued a directive to patch a high-severity vulnerability in Zyxel GS1900 series switches that is actively exploited for data theft. The flaw allows attackers to exfiltrate sensitive information. Zyxel has released a firmware update; administrators should apply it immediately to mitigate the risk.

title: Russia Restricts Mobile Internet, Hindering Drone Attack Warnings
headline: Russia Restricts Mobile Internet, Hindering Drone Attack Warnings
summary: Russia’s tightening of mobile internet and cellular services is preventing citizens from receiving timely warnings about Ukrainian drone and missile attacks. The restrictions limit access to emergency alerts and real‑time information, increasing risk to civilians during ongoing conflicts.
